messages.author: 061e4134cde5bdc7
messages.subject: RN model
parts:
Hy everyone,
I'm interested in understanding how the occupation pattern of some mammaliam species changes in detriment of some spatial variables. I was using the single season model until starts reading about RN models. It seems makes sense to consider abundance heterogenity in my presence/absence data.
But, after reading so many articles in both parametrization, maybe I got a little confused and the concepts are becoming less clear and more merged in my mind... 
My first difficult is undestand how a space variable, e.g. the edge of a protected area which influenced the occurrence of a given species (in single season Mackenzie models) are now influencing the individual in the RN models? It was make sense fitting models with psi(covar)p(covar), but with RN model, I am not sure if makes sense fitting models like lambda(edge)r(edge). Another issue...Is it any sense derivate the psi value from lambda or should I leave the information on abundance level? If is this a option. Are there any R function where is it possible to get the SE and confidente interval information, than simple use the transformation formula?
Hope I have been able to reasonably explain my doubts,
Regards,
Marina

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] RN model
parts:
hi Marina,
 
 In the RN model the occupancy probability psi is directly related to the abundance parameters according to psi = Pr(N>0) = 1-exp(-lambda) 
so, in the RN model, any covariate on lambda influences directly the occcupancy probability.
 
 Normally a spatial variable should influence lambda in the RN model but it would be possible to model such a variable on both lambda and the detection parameter r.  (a relevant paper is:
Kéry, M. (2008). Estimating abundance from bird counts: binomial mixture models uncover complex covariate relationships.
The Auk, 125(2), 336-345.
)
 
There are not R functions in unmarked to get SEs for the occupancy probability from the RN model, I think you would have to use the delta method and conjure them up yourself.
 
regards,
andy
